items.note: The prompt says exports can reach about 2 million rows and that memory use matters. It also says not to load all rows into memory at once.
The prompt says the signature `export_orders_csv(db, path)` must stay identical. It doesn't give the reason (three callers), but the requirement itself is stated.
The prompt gives the exact header `id,customer_name,total,created_at` and says the column order and value formats must stay identical.
The 'Must stay identical' section includes 'No new dependencies', and the prompt also says to use the standard library only.
The prompt names the N+1 query, one `SELECT name FROM customers` per order row, as the known main cause.
The prompt says to write each row to the file as it is produced and not build one big string.
The prompt says customer names can contain commas, so values need proper CSV quoting.
The prompt says to run the existing tests in tests/test_export.py and treats a passing run as part of being done.
The prompt asks for a minimal change, says not to restructure the module, and says to make no changes beyond what the task needs.

invented: The prompt says 'Customers may be missing for some orders' as if it were a fact about the data. That claim isn't in the request, the material or the answers. The current code would raise an error on a missing customer, so the instruction to keep 'the current behaviour' also has no basis.
